NoteTexAccessor::strip_delims¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::strip_delims() const

Remove Math Markers, Retain Their Payload¶

strip_delims() removes the six lexical math markers $, $$, \(, \), \[, and \] from every Text cell. Formula content and all other TeX commands remain in source form. Use it when delimiters are unwanted but the mixture of prose and formulas must stay in its original order; use math_only() when only formula bodies should survive, or text_only() when formulas themselves should disappear.

This is deliberately a lexical transform, not a balance check. Every recognized marker is removed independently, including an unmatched opening or closing marker. Escaped literal dollars (\$) and doubled-backslash text are preserved. The method does not remove braces, evaluate commands, insert spaces, or collapse existing whitespace, so adjacent source separated only by a marker can become adjacent in the result.

The operation is out-of-place, idempotent, and preserves rank, shape, cell order, and Text dtype. Undefined input propagates; defined non-Text Notes reject. It performs one linear scan and allocates at most the retained byte count for each cell.

Example 1: Every Delimiter Form And Escaped Literals¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A $x+1$ B $$y$$ C \(z\) D \[q\])",
    R"(price \$5; escaped \\(literal\\); unmatched $tail)",
    "plain text"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_delims() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A x+1 B y C z D q", "price \\$5; escaped \\\\(literal\\\\); unmatched tail", "plain text"]

The unmatched dollar is still a delimiter token and disappears. The escaped dollar and doubled backslashes are literal source and remain.

Example 2: Shape And Idempotence¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"$a$", R"(\(b\))", R"(\$3)", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_delims();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_delims()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b"], 
  ["\\$3", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
idempotent=true

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_delims().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_delims();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip delims Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip delims Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • add_math_delimiters: wrap an undelimited cell as one formula.

  • balance_math_delims: repair unmatched math markers.

  • math_only: project each cell onto its formula bodies.
